log.a: Statistical significance is often confused with the probability that a hypothesis is true: a p-value instead measures how probable results at least as extreme as those observed would be under a specified null model. A concrete diagnostic is to ask whether p = 0.03 means there is a 3% chance the null hypothesis is true; answering yes reveals the confusion.
log.b: Python prints [0, 2, 2, 4], because round() uses ties-to-even for exact halfway cases. round(2.675, 2) returns 2.67 because 2.675 is represented in binary floating point slightly below its decimal value, so it is not exactly halfway and rounds downward.
